content: {"summary":"The April 2025 PAYAPI‑E1042 errors were caused by pgx client‑side pool exhaustion, while the October 2025 errors stemmed from PgBouncer server‑side queue saturation and query_wait_timeout errors.","likely_cause":"Different pooling layers: client‑side pgx pool vs server‑side PgBouncer pool","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"April 2025 incident was caused by pgx client pool exhaustion due to long‑running queries on payments‑db‑01, filling the 40‑connection pools on two pods.","evidence_ids":["INC-0035#2","INC-0035#0"],"quote":"A connection returns to the pool when its query finishes, so long-running queries on payments-db-01 keep connections out."},{"text":"October 2025 incident involved PgBouncer queue saturation, with query_wait_timeout errors and both bouncers reaching capacity, causing PAYAPI‑E1042.","evidence_ids":["INC-0095#0","INC-0095#1"],"quote":"the bouncer log carries `pooler error: query_wait_timeout`."}],"next_checks":["Review long‑running query logs from payments‑db‑01 for the April incident","Examine PgBouncer queue length and CPU usage metrics for the October incident","Confirm pool size configurations for pgx and PgBouncer"]}
